budgetSummaryNote: Designed around affordable supermarket staples (bulk oats, eggs, rice, beans, peanut butter, milk, chicken leg quarters, ground beef, bananas, frozen veggies) — typically ~$45–$65/week per athlete depending on local grocery prices.

goalModes.label: Add Good Weight (Clean Mass)
goalModes.summary: For lighter DEs/DTs trying to add 10–20 lbs of functional strength without getting sluggish.
goalModes.macroFocus: High protein (1g per lb target bodyweight) + generous clean carbs around lifts + calorie-dense budget fats.

goalModes.label: Trim Bad Weight & Keep Strength
goalModes.summary: For heavier DTs/NTs converting soft weight into speed, conditioning, and lean muscle.
goalModes.macroFocus: High protein (keep muscle) + controlled carbs timed before/after workouts + extra veggies for fullness.

goalModes.label: Maintain Weight & Peak Speed
goalModes.summary: For linemen already at ideal playing weight focusing on recovery and explosive output.
goalModes.macroFocus: Balanced protein, steady carbs on training days, and consistent hydration.

habits.title: Eat a Real Protein Source at Every Meal
habits.target: 4–5 feedings/day (eggs, chicken, beef, tuna, milk, Greek yogurt, beans)
habits.whyItMatters: Muscles only rebuild from heavy squats and benches when amino acids are available throughout the day.
habits.highSchoolTip: Hard-boil 12 eggs on Sunday night so breakfast or after-school protein takes 30 seconds.

habits.title: Hydrate Early (Half Bodyweight in Oz + Electrolytes)
habits.target: 80–120+ oz water daily (carry a 32 oz bottle at school)
habits.whyItMatters: Even 2% dehydration drops sprint speed, vertical power, and mental sharpness in class and practice.
habits.highSchoolTip: Fill a reusable jug before 1st period; finish 1 jug by lunch and 1 more before dinner.

habits.title: Fuel 45–60 Min Before Lifting or Running
habits.target: Fast-digesting carbs + light protein (banana + PB toast, or oats)
habits.whyItMatters: Skipping lunch and lifting on empty tanks bar speed on Day 2 Lower Body and Day 3 Explosive work.
habits.highSchoolTip: Keep a PB&J sandwich or two bananas + granola bar in your gym bag.

habits.title: Post-Workout Recovery Within 45 Minutes
habits.target: 25–40g protein + 40–70g carbs (chocolate milk + banana, or tuna/rice)
habits.whyItMatters: Kicks off muscle repair immediately and prevents late-night junk food binges.
habits.highSchoolTip: 16–20 oz chocolate milk is one of the cheapest, easiest post-lift recovery shakes in high school.

habits.title: Cut Soda, Sweet Tea & Energy Drinks
habits.target: Zero regular sodas or high-sugar energy cans
habits.whyItMatters: Liquid sugar adds slow belly fat, crashes energy in 4th period, and hurts recovery sleep.
habits.highSchoolTip: Swap for cold water with a squeeze of lemon/lime or milk at meals.

habits.title: 2+ Fist-Sized Servings of Vegetables/Fruit Daily
habits.target: Frozen broccoli, carrots, spinach, bananas, apples, or oranges
habits.whyItMatters: Micronutrients, potassium, and fiber keep joints recovering and digestion running smoothly.
habits.highSchoolTip: Frozen steamer bags of broccoli or mixed veggies cost ~$1.25 and microwave in 4 minutes.

habits.title: Bring Backup Food to School
habits.target: 2 packed snacks on top of school lunch
habits.whyItMatters: A single small school cafeteria tray is rarely enough fuel for a 210–270 lb teenager.
habits.highSchoolTip: Pack 2 PB&J sandwiches, a bag of trail mix/peanuts, and an apple in a gallon zip bag.

habits.title: Protect 8–9 Hours of Sleep
habits.target: Phone away 30 min before bed; consistent wake time
habits.whyItMatters: Growth hormone and nervous system recovery happen during deep sleep — you get stronger sleeping, not lifting.
habits.highSchoolTip: Do homework right after practice so you aren't up past midnight.

mealSlots.name: Power Breakfast: Eggs, Oats & Banana
mealSlots.purpose: Kickstart protein synthesis and load steady carbs for morning classes.

foods.food: Rolled Oats cooked with Milk or Water + Cinnamon

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 1 cup dry oats + 1 cup whole milk

foods.budgetSwap: Store-brand 42 oz tub of rolled oats lasts 2+ weeks

foods.food: Banana + Peanut Butter stirred into oats

mealSlots.prepTip: Short on time? Make Overnight Oats in a jar the night before and grab hard-boiled eggs on the way out.

mealSlots.name: Double-Protein School & Packed Lunch
mealSlots.purpose: Bridge the long gap between morning classes and afternoon training.

foods.food: Tuna Salad or Shredded Chicken Wrap / Sandwiches

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 2 cans tuna (or 6 oz chicken) on 4 slices whole wheat bread + light mayo
portionByGoal.lean-strength: 2 cans tuna (or 6 oz chicken) in 2 high-fiber tortillas + mustard/hot sauce
portionByGoal.maintain: 1.5–2 cans tuna (or 5 oz chicken) on 2–3 slices bread

foods.budgetSwap: Canned chunk light tuna (~$1.00/can) or leftover roasted chicken thighs
Buy 3 lb bag of apples or whole carrots instead of pre-cut snack packs
School cafeteria milk carton + large 32 oz tub of yogurt portioned at home

mealSlots.prepTip: If you buy school lunch, always grab the main meat entree + extra milk + fruit, and add a packed PB&J from your backpack.

mealSlots.name: Pre-Workout Locker-Room Fuel
mealSlots.purpose: Top off glycogen for explosive squats, cleans, and 10-yard sprints.

foods.food: Peanut Butter & Jelly on Whole Wheat Bread

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 1 full PB&J sandwich (2 tbsp PB + 1 tbsp jelly)
portionByGoal.maintain: 1 light PB&J or 2 rice cakes + PB

foods.budgetSwap: Store-brand 100% whole wheat loaf + bulk PB

foods.food: Banana + 16 oz Water with Pinch of Salt
foods.budgetSwap: Bananas average ~$0.25 each — cheapest sports carb on earth

mealSlots.prepTip: Never eat heavy greasy fast food right before training — keep it simple carbs + easy digestion.

mealSlots.name: Post-Lift Recovery Shake / Snack
mealSlots.purpose: Halt muscle breakdown and replenish energy fast.

foods.food: Cold Chocolate Milk (or Milk + Scoop Whey if owned)

portionByGoal.lean-strength: 12–16 oz low-fat milk + 1 scoop whey (or 1 cup Greek yogurt)

foods.budgetSwap: Half-gallon of store-brand chocolate milk costs ~$2.50 and gives 3–4 servings
Store-brand pretzel bag (~$2.00 for a full week)

mealSlots.prepTip: Put chocolate milk in an insulated bottle with ice so it's cold right after your last sprint.

mealSlots.name: Trench Builder Dinner: Meat, Rice/Potatoes & Greens
mealSlots.purpose: Main muscle-building meal of the day using budget family staples.

foods.food: Baked Chicken Thighs/Leg Quarters OR 85/15 Ground Beef

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 8 oz cooked chicken thighs or ground beef
portionByGoal.lean-strength: 6–7 oz trimmed chicken breast/thighs or drained 90/10 beef
portionByGoal.maintain: 6–7 oz chicken thighs or ground beef

foods.budgetSwap: Chicken leg quarters ($0.99–$1.49/lb) and family-pack ground beef are half the cost of steaks

foods.food: White/Brown Rice + Black/Pinto Beans OR Baked Potatoes

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 2 cups cooked rice + 1/2 cup beans (or 2 medium potatoes)
portionByGoal.lean-strength: 1 cup rice + 1/2 cup beans (or 1 medium potato)

foods.budgetSwap: 5–10 lb bag of rice + dry beans = pennies per serving and extra fiber/protein

foods.food: Steamed Frozen Broccoli or Mixed Vegetables
foods.budgetSwap: Frozen broccoli florets (~$1.25/bag) have identical nutrients to fresh with zero spoilage

mealSlots.prepTip: Cook 4 lbs of chicken or ground beef + a big pot of rice on Sunday and Wednesday for grab-and-go bowls.

mealSlots.name: Overnight Muscle Repair Snack
mealSlots.purpose: Slow-digesting casein protein feeds recovering muscles overnight.

foods.food: Cottage Cheese OR Plain Greek Yogurt + Frozen Berries

portionByGoal.clean-mass: 1 cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt + 1 tbsp PB + berries
portionByGoal.lean-strength: 3/4 cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt + berries
portionByGoal.maintain: 1 cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt

foods.budgetSwap: 32 oz tub of store-brand cottage cheese or Greek yogurt (~$3.50 for 4 nights)

mealSlots.prepTip: Keep this light and cool so you sleep deeply without stomach discomfort.
